extracted.intended_audience: theology students, seminary students, and scholars of Catholic doctrine
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of Catholic doctrinal standards and distinctions concerning divine grace (its kinds, effects, relation to free will, and contested propositions as treated by Aquinas, Augustine, the Council of Trent, Vatican I, and later theologians). Intended to guide theological judgment about orthodox teaching on grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classifications of causes relevant to grace
rubrics_metrics.description: Causa formalis; Causa efficiens; Causa meritoria; Causa materialis; Causalitas moralis; Causalitas physica; Causa finalis inadaequata; Causa finalis adaequata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the distinct categories of cause used to analyze divine action and the operation of grace; these categories are the framework for distinguishing how God’s causality operates (formally, efficiently, meritoriously, materially, morally, physically, and with respect to final adequacy).

rubrics_metrics.name: God acts by external exhortations and internal inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: "Visorum suasionibus agit Deus, ut velimus et ut credamus, sive extrinsecus per evangelicas exhortationes sive intrinsecus..."; "Interior magister est, qui docet; Christus docet, inspiratio ipsius docet."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrinal standard that divine influence on the will and intellect can be both extrinsic (preaching, exhortation) and intrinsic (interior inspiration or illuminating grace). Emphasizes that external preaching alone is insufficient unless interior grace opens the soul to receive it (supporting citations: Tract. in Ioa., Summa, Ripalda).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gratia inspirationis (terminological clarification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term gratia inspirationis, in Augustine and Trent (Sess. VI, can. 3), sometimes denotes the immediate illuminating grace of the mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies usage: 'gratia inspirationis' may signify immediate intellectual illumination rather than only a will-grace; important for correct interpretation of patristic and conciliar texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two senses of gratuitous divine assistance (motion vs habitual gift)
rubrics_metrics.description: In one way a gratuitous effect in man is not a quality but a motion of the soul (a moving act); in another way man is aided by a habitual infused gift which is a quality of the soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draws on Summa Theol. (1a 2ae, qu. 110, art. 2). Use this distinction when classifying whether grace is to be treated as an actuating movement or as an infused habitual quality; cited authorities (Palmieri, Pesch, Schiffini) discuss implications and acceptance among Thomists and Molinists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five effects of grace (classification of grace's effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sunt autem quinque effectus gratiae in nobis, quorum primus est ut anima sanetur; secundus ut bonum velit; tertius est ut bonum quod vult efficaciter operetur; quartus est ut in bono perseveret; quintus est ut ad gloriam perveniat."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A canonical Thomistic taxonomy (Summa 1a 2ae, qu. 111, art. 3) used to evaluate what particular grace is said to accomplish in the soul — healing, willing, efficacious acting, perseverance, and final glorification. Useful for adjudicating claims about whether a given grace is prevenient, cooperating, sufficient, or efficacious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification in adults begins with prevenient grace (Council of Trent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conc. Trident., Sess. VI, cap. 5: "Declarat praeterea, ipsius justificationis exordium in adultis a Dei per Iesum Christum praeveniente gratia sumendum esse..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official conciliar standard: the beginning (exordium) of justification in adults is to be taken as from God's prevenient vocation/grace; doctrinally central when evaluating teachings on the order of grace and human cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free will cooperates with divine motion (condemnation of the contrary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sess. VI, can. 4: "Si quis dixerit, liberum hominis arbitrium a Deo motum et excitatum nihil cooperari Deo... neque posse dissentire, si velit, anathema sit."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council of Trent anathematizes the claim that a divinely moved human will does not cooperate with God or that it cannot resist; establishes that human freedom and divine motion/assistance are compatible and that denial is heretical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between sufficient grace and efficacious grace
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussions and critiques of the notion of 'gratia sufficiens' versus 'gratia efficax', including condemnations of extreme views that render sufficient grace per se impotent (e.g., called a 'monstrum' in De Grat. Christi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to evaluate positions about whether sufficient grace necessarily results in action; the text reports theological disputes and papal/concilial censures (e.g., Pope Alexander VIII condemned certain assertions) and cites authorities (Schiffini, Palmieri) refuting errors about sufficiency and efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charity (caritas) is essential for a morally good act
rubrics_metrics.description: "Ubi non est dilectio, nullum bonum opus imputatur..."; "Praecepta dilectionis... ut quidquid se putaverit homo facere bene, si fiat sine caritate, nullo modo fiat bene."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrinal criterion (Augustinian/Thomistic): moral goodness of works depends on charity; external conformity to precept without charity is not truly good. Important when judging the moral value of acts (including works of non-believers) and in polemics against views that attribute salvific value to mere natural virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural reason can, by created things, know God (Vatican I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conc. Vat., Sess. III, De Revel., can. 1: "Si quis dixerit, Deum... per ea, quae facta sunt, naturali rationis humanae lumine certo cognosci non posse, anathema sit."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conciliar standard asserting that God is knowable by natural reason through consideration of creation (the 'proofs' of God); relevant when assessing claims about the limits of natural theology and the relation between faith and reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not all pre-justification works are necessarily sins (Trent's condemnation of the contrary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conc. Trident., Sess. VI, can. 7: condemns the assertion that 'opera omnia, quae ante iustificationem fiunt, ... vere esse peccata...' (i.e., that all works before justification are true sins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrinal rule rejecting the claim that every human action prior to justification is necessarily sinful; used to evaluate opinions about the state of the unbaptized, the morally good acts of pagans, and the effects of original sin on natural virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemnations of specific Jansenist/Baius propositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple condemned propositions are cited (e.g., Prop. Baii Damn. 27: 'Liberum arbitrium sine gratiae Dei adiutorio nonnisi ad peccandum valet.'; Prop. Baii Damn. 34, 36, 37, 38, 59, etc.), and various papal and conciliar censures (Alex. VIII, Unigenitus) are referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cluster of negative doctrinal standards: these condemnations mark positions considered heretical or erroneous about grace, freedom, the nature of love, and human action. The text uses them as normative benchmarks when distinguishing orthodox teaching from Jansenist/Baiist errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of prayer and petition for grace
rubrics_metrics.description: De Natura et Gratia, c. 48: faithful pray 'Ne nos inferas in tentationem' because man needs grace to be freed from vices and to be healed; 'Orare sinatur, ut sanetur.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical-theological standard: prayer is necessary to obtain grace; theological treatments (Suarez, Bellarmine) discussed as exhaustive treatments of the necessity of grace and prayer — relevant for assessing pastoral and devotional claims about attaining grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: On natural love vs supernatural charity (amor naturalis vs amor gratuitus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prop. Baii Damn. 34 & 36 and related commentary: distinction between a natural love of God (amor naturalis) and the gratuitous love by which God is loved as beatificator; some condemnations say the distinction as posed by some is vain and erroneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for evaluating assertions about the capacity of natural faculties to love God in a way that would yield justification; used to judge speculative claims on whether natural love could be sufficient for salvation or improperly minimize the need for supernatural charity.
